display.title: Haggadah in Yiddish 3b: Matzah, Maror, Korech, the Afikoman and Eliyahu's Cup
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Haggadah class for children from Rachtzah to opening the door for Eliyahu HaNavi, with the Chabad custom of not letting matzah get wet.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish to children, this class covers the second half of the Seder. At Rachtzah we wash with a brachah and do not speak. For Motzi-Matzah all three matzos are held for Hamotzi and two for Al Achilas Matzah, and a kezayis is eaten while leaning. Maror, romaine lettuce with horseradish dipped in charoses, is eaten without leaning because it recalls the bitter times. Korech is the sandwich Hillel made in the days of the Beis HaMikdash. At Shulchan Orech the festive meal begins with the egg in salt water, roasted meat is avoided, and extra wine may be drunk only during the meal. Tzafun is the afikoman, the Seder's dessert, eaten before midnight with nothing after it except the last two cups. At Barech everyone has a cup, Eliyahu's cup is filled, and mayim acharonim is only on the fingertips. The teacher explains the Chabad custom of keeping matzah dry all Pesach except Acharon shel Pesach, with an anecdote about a Rebbe wiping his fork after every bite, then the third cup, pouring the fourth, and opening the door for Eliyahu HaNavi with a nigun.
display.lesson: Each step of the Seder has its reason; doing the mitzvos carefully, like keeping the matzah dry, shows our love for them.

segments.title: Rachtzah and Motzi-Matzah
segments.summary: Washing with a brachah, holding the matzos for the two brachos, and eating a kezayis while leaning.

segments.title: Maror
segments.summary: Lettuce and horseradish dipped in charoses, eaten without leaning.

segments.title: Korech: Hillel's sandwich
segments.summary: Matzah and maror together, as Hillel ate them with the Korban Pesach.

segments.title: Shulchan Orech: the Yom Tov meal
segments.summary: No roasted meat, the egg recalling the Korban Chagigah, and when extra wine is allowed.

segments.title: Tzafun: the afikoman
segments.summary: The afikoman is the dessert, eaten before midnight, with nothing eaten or drunk after it.

segments.title: Barech, Eliyahu's cup and mayim acharonim
segments.summary: A cup for everyone, filling Eliyahu's cup, and washing only the fingertips.

segments.title: Keeping the matzah dry
segments.summary: The Chabad custom of not letting matzah get wet, except on Acharon shel Pesach, and not calling others' custom a sin.

segments.title: A Rebbe wipes his fork
segments.summary: A Rebbe, the teacher thinks the Rebbe Maharash, wiped his fork after every bite so no matzah crumb would get wet.

segments.title: Bentching and the third cup
segments.summary: Holding the cup during bentching, Retzei and the Yom Tov Harachaman, and drinking the third cup.

segments.title: The fourth cup and opening the door
segments.summary: Pouring the fourth cup and going to the door with candles for Eliyahu HaNavi.

segments.title: Nigun at the door
segments.summary: The nigun sung while the door is open, before Shefoch Chamascha.

relations.note: 'hg3a' ends with the second cup; this part opens with Rachtzah.

quality.notes: Ends during the nigun at the door, before Shefoch Chamascha is said. The anecdote's Rebbe is named hesitantly ('I think it was the Rebbe Maharash').

identity_guesses.evidence_quote: No name, sign-off or credit in the recording; the teacher addresses 'kinderlach' throughout.

needs_human_review: Teacher not named; possibly Rabbi Yosef Goldstein (same archive), unconfirmed.
